name: SHAFT
full_name: Search for Halo Axions with Ferromagnetic Toroids
summary: A broadband ultralight-axion prototype using ferromagnetic toroidal cores to enhance the static magnetic field.
detection_principle: Axion electromagnetic coupling generates a weak oscillating field in a static magnetic field, enhanced by iron–nickel powder cores and read out by a SQUID flux sensor.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2020 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for axion-like dark matter with ferromagnets

collaboration.name: SHAFT Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Axion–photon coupling limits were obtained, reaching approximately 4.0×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ at 20 peV (95% CL).

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
